stem: Which imaging modality is the gold standard for reliably diagnosing hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
explanation: Ultrasound is the gold standard for diagnosing hypertrophic pyloric stenosis because it can directly measure pyloric muscle thickness and channel length and show failure of the pylorus to open normally.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ultrasound is the gold standard for diagnosing hypertrophic pyloric stenosis and allows direct measurement of pyloric muscle thickness and channel length.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a plain abdominal X-ray may show nonspecific gastric distension but cannot confirm hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because CT is not the preferred test in infants and is unnecessary when ultrasound can diagnose the condition accurately without radiation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because MRI is not the standard diagnostic test for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis and is impractical compared with ultrasound.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because an upper gastrointestinal contrast study may be used in selected cases but ultrasound is the first-line gold standard test.

source.hint: This modality allows for real-time observation of the pyloric channel failing to open.
